title: If I'd known, I'd have come
goal: Sēf tells you that you missed the lecture where the professor went over the exam; say what you'd have done if you'd known
tip: lō + a past verb looks back at something that didn't happen: lō dirēt 'if I'd known'. The result is chān + a past verb: lō dirēt, chān yīt badri 'if I'd known, I'd have come early'. chān never changes; the past verb shows who: chān ʿiraft 'you'd have known'.
grammar: past counterfactual: lō + past verb, chān + past verb
dialogue: A
وينك اليوم؟ الدكتور حل ويانا أسئلة الامتحانات القديمة كلها!
wēnak il-yōm? id-daktōr ḥall wiyyāna asʼilat il-imtiḥānāt il-gadīma killha!
Where were you today? The professor went through all the old exam papers with us!
B
لا والله! كنت نايم، المنبه ما رن
la wallāh! kint nāyim, il-munabbih ma rann
No way! I was asleep, the alarm didn't go off.
A
خسارة! لو حضرت، جان عرفت شو بيكون في الامتحان
khasāra! lō ḥaẓart, chān ʿiraft shu biykūn fi l-imtiḥān
What a shame! If you'd been there, you'd have known what's going to be in the exam.
B
لو دريت، جان ييت من الساعة سبع!
lō dirēt, chān yīt min is-sāʿa sabʿ!
If I'd known, I'd have come at seven!
A
ترا طرشت لك في القروب أمس. لو شفت تلفونك، جان دريت
tara ṭarrasht-lak fi l-grūb ams. lō shift tilifōnak, chān dirēt
I sent it to you in the group yesterday, you know. If you'd looked at your phone, you'd have known.
B
تلفوني كان طافي. البطارية خلصت
tilifōni kān ṭāfi. il-baṭṭāriyya khilṣat
My phone was off. The battery died.
A
ما عليه، لا تحاتي. كتبت كل شي قاله
ma ʿalēh, la tḥāti. kitabt kill shay gālah
Never mind, don't worry. I wrote down everything he said.
B
صج؟ والله لو ما عندي ربيع مثلك، جان ضعت!
ṣij? wallāh lō ma ʿindi rbīʿ mithlak, chān ẓiʿt!
Really? Honestly, if I didn't have a friend like you, I'd be lost!
A
يلا، تعال المكتبة وأشرح لك
yalla, taʿāl il-maktaba w ashraḥ-lak
Come on, come to the library and I'll explain it to you.
items: if I'd known; if you'd known (to a man)
to a woman: lō dirēti (لو دريتي)
if you'd been there, if you'd come (to class) (to a man); if I'd been there
to a woman: lō ḥaẓarti (لو حضرتي)
you'd have known (to a man); I'd have known
to a woman: chān ʿirafti (جان عرفتي)
if you'd looked at your phone (to a man)
to a woman: lō shifti tilifōnich (لو شفتي تلفونج)
it was off, it was switched off (m.)
a feminine thing: kānat ṭāfya (كانت طافية)
the battery died, the battery ran out
I'd be lost, I'd have been lost
old exam papers, past exam questions

title: Good thing you saved a copy
goal: At the office, your laptop dies before a meeting; Maryam saved a copy. Thank her and say what would have happened
tip: Put ma after lō for 'if … hadn't': lō ma ḥafaẓti nuskha 'if you hadn't saved a copy'. Put ma after chān for 'wouldn't have': chān ma khallaṣna 'we wouldn't have finished'. zēn inn- + an ending is 'good thing (that)': zēn innich ḥafaẓtīha.
grammar: negative counterfactual: lō ma + past verb, chān ma + past verb
dialogue: B
مريم، اللابتوب طفى فجأة، والعرض كله راح!
Maryam, il-lābtōb ṭafa fajʼa, w il-ʿarẓ killah rāḥ!
Maryam, the laptop suddenly died, and the whole presentation's gone!
A
لا تخاف، حفظت نسخة عندي أمس
la tkhāf, ḥafaẓt nuskha ʿindi ams
Don't panic, I saved a copy on mine yesterday.
B
الحمد لله! لو ما حفظتي نسخة، جان ضاع شغل أسبوع كامل
il-ḥamdu lillāh! lō ma ḥafaẓti nuskha, chān ẓāʿ shughul usbūʿ kāmil
Thank God! If you hadn't saved a copy, a whole week's work would have been lost.
A
هيه، ومن غيرها جان ما خلصنا قبل الاجتماع
hē, w min ghērha chān ma khallaṣna gabl il-ijtimāʿ
Yes, and without it we wouldn't have finished before the meeting.
B
زين إنج حفظتيها! أنا ما حفظت شي
zēn innich ḥafaẓtīha! ana ma ḥafaẓt shay
Good thing you saved it! I hadn't saved anything.
A
كم مرة قلت لك؟ احفظ كل عشر دقايق!
cham marra gilt-lak? iḥfaẓ kill ʿashr dagāyig!
How many times have I told you? Save every ten minutes!
B
صح، غلطتي. لو سمعت كلامج، جان ما صار شي
ṣaḥḥ, ghalṭati. lō simaʿt kalāmich, chān ma ṣār shay
True, my fault. If I'd listened to you, nothing would have happened.
A
المهم، تعال نكمل من عندي
il-muhimm, taʿāl nkammil min ʿindi
Anyway, come on, let's carry on from mine.
B
ماشي. ومن اليوم، بحفظ كل شي مرتين!
māshi. w min il-yōm, baḥfaẓ kill shay marratēn!
OK. And from today, I'll save everything twice!
items: if you hadn't saved (it) (to a woman)
to a man: lō ma ḥafaẓt (لو ما حفظت)
a feminine thing: chān ẓāʿat (جان ضاعت)
to a man: zēn innak (زين إنك)
I saved a copy; you saved a copy (to a man)
to a woman: ḥafaẓti nuskha (حفظتي نسخة)
if I'd listened to you (to a woman) (lit. heard your words)
to a man: lō simaʿt kalāmak (لو سمعت كلامك)
how many times have I told you? (to a man)
to a woman: cham marra gilt-lich? (كم مرة قلت لج؟); (recognise)

title: If it weren't for you
goal: The day after your car battery died on the road at night, thank Sēf for coming to help, and take his advice
tip: lōla means 'if it weren't for': lōla z-zaḥma 'if it weren't for the traffic'. It takes endings: lōlāk 'if it weren't for you (m.)', lōlāch (f.). The result is chān + a past verb: lōlāk, chān ẓallēt hnāk. lōla allāh thumm inta is a warm way to say thanks.
grammar: lōla 'if it weren't for' + chān + past verb
dialogue: A
ها، شو صار في السيارة؟ ركبوا لك بطارية يديدة؟
hā, shu ṣār fi s-sayyāra? rakkbaw-lak baṭṭāriyya yidīda?
So, what happened with the car? Did they put a new battery in for you?
B
هيه، الصبح في الكراج. الحمد لله
hē, iṣ-ṣubḥ fi l-karāj. il-ḥamdu lillāh
Yes, this morning at the garage. Thank God.
A
أمس كنت خايف عليك، الشارع كان ظلام
ams kint khāyif ʿalēk, ish-shāriʿ kān ẓalām
Last night I was worried about you, the road was dark.
B
والله لولاك، جان ظليت هناك لين الصبح
wallāh lōlāk, chān ẓallēt hnāk lēn iṣ-ṣubḥ
Honestly, if it weren't for you, I'd have stayed stuck there till morning.
A
لا يا ريّال، ما سويت شي. أي واحد جان سوى نفس الشي
la yā rayyāl, ma sawwēt shay. ay wāḥid chān sawwa nafs ish-shay
Come on, man, I didn't do anything. Anyone would have done the same.
B
لا، لولا الله ثم انت، جان ما دريت شو أسوي
la, lōla allāh thumm inta, chān ma dirēt shu asawwi
No, if it weren't for God and then you, I wouldn't have known what to do.
A
بس ترا قلت لك من شهرين: جان غيرتها من زمان!
bas tara gilt-lak min shahrēn: chān ghayyart-ha min zamān!
But I told you two months ago: you should have changed it ages ago!
B
صح كلامك. جان غيرتها، بس نسيت
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak. chān ghayyart-ha, bas nisēt
You're right. I should have changed it, but I forgot.
A
ما عليه، الحمد لله على كل حال
ma ʿalēh, il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala kill ḥāl
Never mind, thank God for everything.
B
والعشا الليلة علي، لا تقول لا!
w il-ʿasha l-lēla ʿalay, la tgūl la!
And dinner tonight's on me, don't say no!
items: if it weren't for you, without you (to a man)
if it weren't for God and then you (warm thanks) (to a man)
to a woman: lōla allāh thumm inti (لولا الله ثم انتي)
I'd have stayed, I'd have been stuck
you should have changed it (f.) (to a man); I should have changed it
to a woman: chān ghayyartīha (جان غيرتيها)
they fitted you (a part), they put in for you (to a man)
thank God for everything, thank God anyway (after something bad)
to a woman: la tgūlīn la (لا تقولين لا)

title: No regrets, uncle
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, he asks if you regret coming to Dubai; say what would have happened if you hadn't
tip: lō ma + a past verb with chān ma answers 'what if I hadn't?': lō ma yīt Dbayy, chān ma tʿallamt il-ʿarabi. chān + an adjective is 'it would have been …': chān aḥsan 'it would have been better'. To an elder, keep yā ʿammi.
grammar: counterfactuals about life choices; chān + adjective
dialogue: A
ها يا ولدي، صار لك سنتين في دبي. ندمت إنك ييت؟
hā yā wildi, ṣār-lak santēn fi Dbayy. nidamt innak yīt?
So, my son, you've been in Dubai two years now. Do you regret coming?
B
لا والله يا عمي، ما ندمت أبد
la wallāh yā ʿammi, ma nidamt abad
No, honestly, uncle, I don't regret it at all.
A
زين. ولو ما ييت، شو جان سويت؟
zēn. w lō ma yīt, shu chān sawwēt?
Good. And if you hadn't come, what would you have done?
B
جان درست في لندن، وجان ما تعلمت العربي
chān darast fi Landan, w chān ma tʿallamt il-ʿarabi
I'd have studied in London, and I wouldn't have learnt Arabic.
A
وجان ما عرفناك! الحمد لله إنك ييت
w chān ma ʿirafnāk! il-ḥamdu lillāh innak yīt
And we'd never have got to know you! Thank God you came.
B
الله يخليك يا عمي. بس مرات أقول: لو اخترت طب، جان أحسن
allāh ykhallīk yā ʿammi. bas marrāt agūl: lō ikhtart ṭibb, chān aḥsan
That's kind of you, uncle. But sometimes I think: if I'd chosen medicine, it would have been better.
A
لا يا ولدي، الهندسة زينة. وبعدين، اللي فات مات
la yā wildi, il-handasa zēna. w baʿdēn, illi fāt māt
No, my son, engineering's good. And anyway, what's past is past.
B
صدقت والله يا عمي
ṣidagt wallāh yā ʿammi
Too true, uncle.
A
تفضل القهوة، وسلم لي على أبوك
tfaẓẓal il-gahwa, w sallim-li ʿala ubūk
Have some coffee, and give my regards to your father.
B
الله يسلمك، يوصل إن شاء الله
allāh ysallmak, yōṣal in shāʼ allāh
Thank you, I'll pass it on.
items: do you regret coming? (to a man)
to a woman: nidamti innich yīti? (ندمتي إنج ييتي؟)
I don't regret it at all, I've never regretted it
what would you have done? (to a man)
to a woman: shu chān sawwēti? (شو جان سويتي؟)
I'd have studied; you'd have studied (to a man)
to a woman: chān darasti (جان درستي)
I wouldn't have learnt; you wouldn't have learnt (to a man)
to a woman: chān ma tʿallamti (جان ما تعلمتي)
we'd never have got to know you (to a man)
to a woman: chān ma ʿirafnāch (جان ما عرفناج); (recognise)
if I'd chosen; if you'd chosen (to a man)
to a woman: lō ikhtarti (لو اخترتي)
what's past is past, let bygones be bygones

title: You should have registered earlier
goal: Sēf missed the course registration; talk about what he and the university should have done, and what he can still do
tip: chān + someone's past verb says what they should have done: chān sajjalt badri 'you should have registered early', chān ṭarrashaw īmēl 'they should have sent an email'. It works for every person: chān sajjalt (I), chān gālaw (they).
grammar: chān + past verb: 'should have' for any person
dialogue: A
خلاص، راحت علي! التسجيل سكر أمس
khalāṣ, rāḥat ʿalay! it-tasjīl sakkar ams
That's it, I've missed out! Registration closed yesterday.
B
أفا! ليش ما سجلت من أول؟
afa! lēsh ma sajjalt min awwal?
Oh no! Why didn't you register earlier?
A
نسيت. والجامعة ما طرشت ولا رسالة!
nisēt. w il-jāmʿa ma ṭarrashat wala risāla!
I forgot. And the university didn't send a single message!
B
والله جان طرشوا إيميل على الأقل
wallāh chān ṭarrashaw īmēl ʿala l-aqall
Honestly, they should have sent an email at least.
A
صح. بس أنا بعد جان سجلت قبل الكل. الغلط مني
ṣaḥḥ. bas ana baʿad chān sajjalt gabl il-kill. il-ghalaṭ minni
True. But I should have registered before everyone too. It's my fault.
B
وكلمت الدكتور؟
w kallamt id-daktōr?
And did you talk to the professor?
A
هيه، يقول: لو ييتني قبل يومين، جان ساعدتك
hē, ygūl: lō yītni gabil yōmēn, chān sāʿadtak
Yes, he says: if you'd come to me two days ago, I'd have helped you.
B
يعني ما في أمل؟
yaʿni ma fī amal?
So there's no hope?
A
في، بس لازم أكتب له إيميل وأشرح له
fī, bas lāzim aktib-lah īmēl w ashraḥ-lah
There is, but I have to write him an email and explain.
B
اكتبه الحين! لا تتريا لين باكر
iktibah il-ḥīn! la titrayya lēn bāchir
Write it now! Don't wait till tomorrow.
items: I've missed out, I've missed my chance
why didn't you register? (to a man)
to a woman: lēsh ma sajjalti? (ليش ما سجلتي؟)
I should have registered; you should have registered (to a man)
to a woman: chān sajjalti (جان سجلتي)
if you'd come to me (to a man)
to a woman: lō yītīni (لو ييتيني); (recognise)
I'd have helped you (to a man)
to a woman: chān sāʿadtich (جان ساعدتج); (recognise)
is there no hope? no chance at all?
to a woman: la titrayyīn (لا تتريين)
task: This week: record a 60-second voice note to Sēf about one thing you'd do differently if you could go back a year. Say what happened, then use lō + a past verb with chān twice (lō dirēt, chān …) and chān + a past verb once for 'I should have' (chān sajjalt …). Listen back once and fix any 'you' ending.

title: If I'd known about the delay
goal: Meet Fahad at Dubai airport after his delayed flight, with Sēf parking the car, and catch his Kuwaiti lō dāri
tip: lō kān (or lō kint) + an adjective or participle is 'if it had been / if I had been': lō kān il-jaww zēn 'if the weather had been good'. Fahad's Kuwaiti lō dāri 'if I'd known' means the same as lō dirēt. lō kān fī wagt 'if there'd been time'.
grammar: counterfactual with lō kān + adjective or participle
dialogue: B
هلا والله بفهد! الحمد لله على السلامة
hala wallāh b-Fahad! il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma
Hello, Fahad! Welcome, good to have you here safe.
A
الله يسلمك. شنو هالرحلة! تأخرت ثلاث ساعات
allāh ysallmak. shinu har-riḥla! taʼakhkharat thalāth sāʿāt
Thanks. What a flight! It was three hours late.
B
ثلاث ساعات؟ لو درينا، جان ما طلعنا من البيت بدري
thalāth sāʿāt? lō dirēna, chān ma ṭilaʿna min il-bēt badri
Three hours? If we'd known, we wouldn't have left the house early.
A
وأنا لو داري، جان قعدت أنام في البيت شوي بعد!
w ana lō dāri, chān gaʿadt anām fi l-bēt shwayy baʿad!
And if I'd known, I'd have stayed at home and slept a bit more!
B
ولو كان في وقت، جان رحنا نتريق قبل
w lō kān fī wagt, chān riḥna nitrayyag gabil
And if there'd been time, we'd have gone for breakfast first.
A
عادي، الحين نروح. وين سيف؟
ʿādi, il-ḥīn nrūḥ. wēn Sēf?
It's fine, we'll go now. Where's Sēf?
B
يصف السيارة. لو كان الجو زين، جان مشينا له
yṣiff is-sayyāra. lō kān il-jaww zēn, chān mishēna lah
He's parking the car. If the weather had been nice, we'd have walked over to him.
A
لا لا، المكيف أحسن! يلا، شلون جان وصلت من غيركم؟
la la, il-mkayyif aḥsan! yalla, shlōn chān wiṣalt min ghērkum?
No, no, the air conditioning's better! Come on, how would I have got there without you guys?
B
جان خذت تاكسي، عادي! حياك الله في دبي
chān khadht tāksi, ʿādi! ḥayyāk allāh fi Dbayy
You'd have taken a taxi, no big deal! Welcome to Dubai.
A
الله يحييك. والله اشتقت لكم!
allāh yḥayyīk. wallāh ishtagt-lkum!
Thank you. I've really missed you guys!
items: we wouldn't have left, we wouldn't have gone out
if I'd known (Kuwait) (said by a man)
a woman says: lō dārya (لو دارية); UAE: lō dirēt; (recognise)
it (f.) was three hours late (a flight)
if there'd been time, if there was time
if the weather had been nice, if the weather were nice
to one man: ishtagt-lak; to one woman: ishtagt-lich

title: I'll have finished by tomorrow
goal: At the office, Maryam asks when your part of the report will be done; promise what you'll have finished, and by when
tip: bakūn + a past verb says what will be done by a certain time: bakūn khallaṣt bāchir 'I'll have finished by tomorrow'. The first verb shows the person and the future (bitkūn, biykūn); the past verb agrees too: biykūn shāfah 'he'll have seen it'. To a woman: bitkūnīn khallaṣti.
dialogue: A
سالم، المدير يبي التقرير يوم الخميس. متى بتكون خلصت حقك؟
Sālim, il-mudīr yabi t-taqrīr yōm il-khamīs. mita bitkūn khallaṣt ḥaggak?
Sālim, the manager wants the report on Thursday. When will you have finished your part?
B
إن شاء الله بكون خلصت باكر الظهر
in shāʼ allāh bakūn khallaṣt bāchir iẓ-ẓuhur
God willing, I'll have finished by tomorrow at midday.
A
زين. وأنا بكون خلصت الأرقام الليلة
zēn. w ana bakūn khallaṣt il-argām il-lēla
Good. And I'll have finished the figures tonight.
B
يعني باكر العصر بيكون التقرير جاهز؟
yaʿni bāchir il-ʿaṣir biykūn it-taqrīr jāhiz?
So tomorrow afternoon the report will be ready?
A
إن شاء الله. بس باكر العصر أنا عندي موعد، لازم أطلع بدري
in shāʼ allāh. bas bāchir il-ʿaṣir ana ʿindi mawʿid, lāzim aṭlaʿ badri
God willing. But tomorrow afternoon I've got an appointment, I have to leave early.
B
ما عليه، أنا بطرشه للمدير. بيكون شافه قبل الخميس
ma ʿalēh, ana baṭarrshah lil-mudīr. biykūn shāfah gabl il-khamīs
No problem, I'll send it to the manager. He'll have seen it before Thursday.
A
ممتاز. وإذا في شي ناقص؟
mumtāz. w idha fī shay nāgiṣ?
Great. And if something's missing?
B
لا تحاتين، بكون راجعته مرتين
la tḥātīn, bakūn rājaʿtah marratēn
Don't worry, I'll have checked it twice.
A
يعطيك العافية
yaʿṭīk il-ʿāfya
Thanks for all your work.
B
الله يعافيج
allāh yʿāfīch
And you.
items: when will you have finished? (to a man)
to a woman: mita bitkūnīn khallaṣti? (متى بتكونين خلصتي؟)
a feminine thing: bitkūn jāhza (بتكون جاهزة)
I'll have checked it (m.), I'll have gone over it
I'll send it (m.) to the manager

title: He must have overslept
goal: Waiting with Sēf for Fahad outside his hotel, guess what has happened to him
tip: biykūn + a past verb is also a guess about now: biykūn nām 'he's probably fallen asleep'. akīd biykūn … is a strong guess: akīd biykūn ṭilaʿ 'he must have left'. Ask with tẓunn: tẓunn biykūn wiṣal? 'do you think he's got there?'
grammar: biykūn + past verb for guesses: 'he'll have, he must have'
dialogue: A
فهد ما يرد. الساعة عشر وما طلع
Fahad ma yrudd. is-sāʿa ʿashr w ma ṭilaʿ
Fahad's not answering. It's ten and he hasn't come out.
B
بيكون نام. أمس سهرنا لين ثنتين
biykūn nām. ams sihirna lēn thintēn
He's probably fallen asleep. We stayed up till two last night.
A
لا، طرش لي رسالة الساعة ثمان. أكيد بيكون طلع من الفندق
la, ṭarrash-li risāla s-sāʿa thamān. akīd biykūn ṭilaʿ min il-fundug
No, he sent me a message at eight. He must have left the hotel.
B
عيل وينه؟ بيكون ضاع؟
ʿayal wēnah? biykūn ẓāʿ?
Then where is he? Has he got lost?
A
تظن؟ أول مرة يي دبي، بس عنده خرايط في تلفونه
tẓunn? awwal marra yiyi Dbayy, bas ʿindah kharāyiṭ fi tilifōnah
You think? It's his first time in Dubai, but he's got maps on his phone.
B
يمكن تلفونه طافي. بتكون البطارية خلصت
yimkin tilifōnah ṭāfi. bitkūn il-baṭṭāriyya khilṣat
Maybe his phone's off. The battery will have died.
A
تظن بيكون وصل المترو؟
tẓunn biykūn wiṣal il-mitrō?
Do you think he'll have got to the metro?
B
شوف، هذاك هو! ياي من المحل وفي إيده كرك
shūf, hādhāk huwa! yāy min il-maḥall w fi īdah karak
Look, there he is! He's coming from the shop with a karak in his hand.
A
الحمد لله! ونحن نقول بيكون صار له شي!
il-ḥamdu lillāh! w niḥin ngūl biykūn ṣār-lah shay!
Thank God! And there we were thinking something must have happened to him!
items: he's probably fallen asleep, he'll have gone to sleep
he must have left, he'll have gone out for sure
has he got lost? he's probably got lost
do you think he'll have got there? (to a man)
to a woman: tẓunnīn biykūn wiṣal? (تظنين بيكون وصل؟)
there he is, that's him (over there)
with a karak in his hand
something must have happened to him
لا بد أنه حدث له شيء

title: It'll probably be packed
goal: Plan a Saturday trip to Hatta with Sēf: guess what the roads, the weather and the place will be like
tip: biykūn + an adjective or noun is 'it'll (probably) be': biykūn zaḥma 'it'll be crowded'. It agrees with what it describes: il-maṭāʿim bitkūn msakkara 'the restaurants will be closed'. With fī: biykūn fī nās wāyid 'there'll be lots of people'.
dialogue: A
شرايك نروح حتا يوم السبت؟
shrāyak nrūḥ Ḥatta yōm is-sabt?
How about going to Hatta on Saturday?
B
فكرة حلوة! بس بيكون زحمة؟
fikra ḥilwa! bas biykūn zaḥma?
Good idea! But will it be crowded?
A
الصبح لا. بس العصر بيكون في ناس وايد
iṣ-ṣubḥ la. bas il-ʿaṣir biykūn fī nās wāyid
Not in the morning. But in the afternoon there'll be lots of people.
B
عيل نطلع الساعة ست؟ الشارع بيكون فاضي
ʿayal niṭlaʿ is-sāʿa sitt? ish-shāriʿ biykūn fāẓi
So shall we leave at six? The road will be empty.
A
هيه، وبنكون هناك قبل ثمان
hē, w binkūn hnāk gabil thamān
Yes, and we'll be there before eight.
B
والجو؟ بيكون حار؟
w il-jaww? biykūn ḥārr?
And the weather? Will it be hot?
A
لا، الحين الجو حلو. بس خذ جاكيت، الصبح بيكون بارد شوي
la, il-ḥīn il-jaww ḥilu. bas khudh jākēt, iṣ-ṣubḥ biykūn bārid shwayy
No, the weather's nice now. But take a jacket, it'll be a bit cold in the morning.
B
زين. والريوق؟ المطاعم بتكون مسكرة الساعة ست
zēn. w ir-riyūg? il-maṭāʿim bitkūn msakkara s-sāʿa sitt
OK. And breakfast? The restaurants will be closed at six.
A
لا تحاتي، أمي بتسوي لنا ريوق. أكيد بيكون وايد!
la tḥāti, ummi bitsawwī-lna riyūg. akīd biykūn wāyid!
Don't worry, my mum's going to make us breakfast. It's bound to be loads!
B
الله يخليها! سلم لي عليها
allāh ykhallīha! sallim-li ʿalēha
Bless her! Say hello to her for me.
items: it'll be crowded, it'll probably be busy
it'll be a bit cold, it'll be chilly
my mum's going to make us breakfast
they'll be closed (shops, restaurants); it (f.)'ll be closed
it's bound to be loads, there'll surely be plenty

title: By the time I'm back
goal: Before the manager travels, he asks the team what will be done by the time he's back; answer for yourself and the team
tip: To a group: bitkūnūn khallaṣtu? 'will you have finished?'. Answer for the team with binkūn khallaṣna 'we'll have finished'. lēn + a present verb gives 'by the time': lēn tirjaʿ 'by the time you're back'. To a manager, keep ṭāl ʿumrak.
grammar: future perfect with every person; lēn 'by the time'
dialogue: A
يا جماعة، أنا مسافر الأسبوع الياي. لين أرجع، بتكونون خلصتوا العرض؟
yā jamāʿa, ana msāfir il-usbūʿ il-yāy. lēn arjaʿ, bitkūnūn khallaṣtu l-ʿarẓ?
Guys, I'm travelling next week. By the time I'm back, will you have finished the presentation?
B
إن شاء الله طال عمرك. بنكون خلصنا يوم الخميس
in shāʼ allāh ṭāl ʿumrak. binkūn khallaṣna yōm il-khamīs
God willing, sir. We'll have finished by Thursday.
A
زين. والأرقام اليديدة؟
zēn. w il-argām il-yidīda?
Good. And the new figures?
B
مريم بتكون خلصتها قبل، وبتطرش لك إيميل
Maryam bitkūn khallaṣat-ha gabil, w bitṭarrish-lak īmēl
Maryam will have finished them before then, and she'll send you an email.
A
وانت؟ شو بتكون سويت لين أرجع؟
w inta? shu bitkūn sawwēt lēn arjaʿ?
And you? What will you have done by the time I'm back?
B
بكون كتبت التقرير، وبكون رتبت الاجتماع
bakūn kitabt it-taqrīr, w bakūn rattabt il-ijtimāʿ
I'll have written the report, and I'll have set up the meeting.
A
ممتاز. والعميل بيكون شاف العرض قبل الاجتماع؟
mumtāz. w il-ʿamīl biykūn shāf il-ʿarẓ gabl il-ijtimāʿ?
Great. And will the client have seen the presentation before the meeting?
B
هيه، بنكون طرشنا له العرض يوم الأحد
hē, binkūn ṭarrashnā-lah il-ʿarẓ yōm il-aḥad
Yes, we'll have sent him the presentation by Sunday.
A
يعطيكم العافية. إذا صار أي شي، طرشوا لي
yaʿṭīkum il-ʿāfya. idha ṣār ay shay, ṭarrshū-li
Thanks for all your work, all of you. If anything happens, message me.
B
الله يعافيك. توصل بالسلامة طال عمرك
allāh yʿāfīk. tōṣal bis-salāma ṭāl ʿumrak
Thank you. Have a safe trip, sir.
items: by the time I'm back, until I get back
will you have finished? (to a group)
to one man: bitkūn khallaṣt?; to one woman: bitkūnīn khallaṣti?
she'll have finished it (f.), she'll have finished them (things)
what will you have done? (to a man)
to a woman: shu bitkūnīn sawwēti? (شو بتكونين سويتي؟)
I set up the meeting; you set up the meeting (to a man)
message me, send me (it) (to a group)
to one man: ṭarrish-li; to one woman: ṭarrshī-li
task: This week: search YouTube for «بودكاست إماراتي» (Emirati podcast) or «سوالف» (chats). Listen until you hear جان or بيكون three times, and write down the sentence around each. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب (UAE) or شنو / مو (Kuwait). If you hear سوف, ليس or هل all the time, it's fuṣḥā: pick another clip.
